metadata.title: Using Machine Learning Approaches to Explore Non-Cognitive Variables Influencing Reading Proficiency in English among Filipino Learners

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Philippines national sample from PISA 2018 (15-year-olds) and reports a two-stage stratified random selection of schools and students. The manuscript describes preprocessing steps (rescaling variables to 0–1, dropping variables with 100% missingness, and imputing remaining missing values with k-nearest neighbors) and then trains/testing ML classifiers using an 80/20 random split and five-fold cross-validation for training performance. No PISA sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are mentioned, and the ML algorithms used (SVM, logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, gradient boosting, random forest, AdaBoost, kNN) are not described as being fit with complex-survey weights. Therefore, the analysis appears to be unweighted and does not explicitly account for PISA’s clustered sampling design beyond the dataset’s original structure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Philippines national sample from the OECD PISA 2018 database. For ML modeling, students were grouped into low vs high reading proficiency using Plausible Value 1 (PV1READ) for reading; low = levels 1b and below, high = levels 1a and better. From the 122 candidate variables, variables with 100% missingness were dropped, and variables with a few missing values were imputed using k-nearest neighbors with k=7. The paper also rescales variable ranges to 0–1 and changes missing tags ("M"/"N") to null values in Python to enable imputation.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (Philippines, English reading proficiency; PV1READ; 15-year-olds)
main_findings.target_variable: Reading proficiency group (low vs high; PV1READ-based)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Best model (SVM): test accuracy = 81.20%, AUC–ROC = 0.89 (confusion matrix reported for low vs high).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data for Filipino 15-year-olds (PV1READ; low = levels 1b and below vs high = levels 1a and better), the study leveraged perceived reading difficulty (SCREADDIFF), exposure to bullying (BEINGBULLIED), mastery persistence (WORKMAST), reading enjoyment (JOYREAD), and ICT resources at home (ICTRES) to predict membership in the low vs high reading proficiency groups, finding that the SVM achieved 81.20% test accuracy and AUC–ROC of 0.89. This indicates that targeted interventions addressing reading self-beliefs, school social climate (e.g., bullying), and home learning resources may improve the identification and support of very low-performing readers, though the results are predictive and not causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes the Philippines’ national sample from PISA 2018 (15-year-olds; reading in English) and constructs a binary target using PV1READ: low proficiency corresponds to PISA reading levels 1b and below, while high corresponds to levels 1a and better. After preprocessing (rescaling variables to 0–1, dropping variables with 100% missingness, and imputing remaining missing values via k-nearest neighbors with k=7), the authors train multiple ML classifiers using an 80/20 random split and evaluate training with five-fold cross-validation. Across SVM, logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, gradient boosting, random forest, AdaBoost, and kNN, the SVM performs best on the test set with 81.20% accuracy and AUC–ROC of 0.89. SHAP is used to interpret the SVM, highlighting SCREADDIFF, BEINGBULLIED, and WORKMAST among the most influential predictors. The analysis appears unweighted (no PISA sampling weights are reported) and uses predictive classification rather than causal identification.
